messages.author: deea3c30b4c8409f
messages.subject: Re: cannot perform: devtools::install_github("hadley/devtools")
parts:
Hi!

You need to be able to build packages from source for installing
devtools from github. You seem to have some version OSX, so you need
either a full XCode installation, or the command line tools for XCode.

You also seem to have a clang installation, you probably installed
this with some other OSX package management tool, like brew or
macports. It is suggested that you use the standard XCode instead of
this.

Gabor

messages.author: deea3c30b4c8409f
messages.subject: Re: cannot perform: devtools::install_github("hadley/devtools")
parts:
Hmmmm, interesting. I can only guess here, because I don't know what
you did exactly, which version of OSX, XCode you have, etc.

Maybe you don't have the XCode command line tools installed? I think
recent XCode versions include the command line tools, but old ones do
not.

If the clang R calls is not the Xcode clang, then check where it is
coming from and remove that directory from your PATH, or uninstall
that clang.

Can you build other R packages from source, e.g. can you run

install.packages("devtools", type="source")

?

Gabor

Well, using clang itself is fine, I agree. But it might come from
brew, or macports, which might be a problem. Anyway, it seems that he
has a broken clang and/or xcode installation, as clang does not find
the standard headers.

Gabor

On Mon, Aug 11, 2014 at 8:39 AM, Hadley Wickham <h.wi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Using clang is what I recommend - so that's unlikely to be the problem.
>
> Hadley
>
> On Sun, Aug 10, 2014 at 4:40 PM, Gábor Csárdi <csardi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> Hmmmm, interesting. I can only guess here, because I don't know what
>> you did exactly, which version of OSX, XCode you have, etc.
>>
>> Maybe you don't have the XCode command line tools installed? I think
>> recent XCode versions include the command line tools, but old ones do
>> not.
>>
>> If the clang R calls is not the Xcode clang, then check where it is
>> coming from and remove that directory from your PATH, or uninstall
>> that clang.
>>
>> Can you build other R packages from source, e.g. can you run
>>
>> install.packages("devtools", type="source")
>>
>> ?
>>
>> Gabor
>>
>> On Sun, Aug 10, 2014 at 9:27 AM, Nicholas Tierney
>> <nicholas...@gmail.com> wrote:

>>>

END OF CODE OUTPUT.

Is there any more information that I can provide that would be helpful to you?

How can I find out if the clang it is calling is not the Xcode clang?

Thank you very much for your help so far.

On Monday, 11 August 2014 06:40:23 UTC+10, Gábor Csárdi wrote:
Hmmmm, interesting. I can only guess here, because I don't know what
you did exactly, which version of OSX, XCode you have, etc.

Maybe you don't have the XCode command line tools installed? I think
recent XCode versions include the command line tools, but old ones do
not.

If the clang R calls is not the Xcode clang, then check where it is
coming from and remove that directory from your PATH, or uninstall
that clang.

Can you build other R packages from source, e.g. can you run

install.packages("devtools", type="source")

?

Gabor

messages.subject: Re: cannot perform: devtools::install_github("hadley/devtools")
parts:
Check where 'clang' is coming from, do you use brew, or macports? If
it is coming from Xcode then maybe your Xcode installation is broken,
and you need to reinstall it.

But this is not devtools specific, it seems that you cannot compile
any R package from source. So maybe it is a good idea to ask on
R-help, or R-sig-mac is even better.

G.
